chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Excellent is the vizier of faith — knowledge; and excellent is the vizier of knowledge — forbearance; and excellent is the vizier of forbearance — gentleness; and excellent is the vizier of gentleness — patience.'

key_terms.الرِّفْقُ: Rifq — gentleness, kindness in action and treatment of others
key_terms.الصَّبْرُ: Sabr — patience, steadfast perseverance especially in adversity
key_terms.الْإِيمَانُ: Iman — faith, the comprehensive belief in God, His Prophets, and Imams
key_terms.الْحِلْمُ: Hilm — forbearance, clemency, the capacity to bear hardship and restrain anger with dignity
key_terms.وَزِيرُ: Vizier — the indispensable minister or support; here used metaphorically for the virtue that enables and strengthens another

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet Muhammad say about the relationship between faith, knowledge, forbearance, gentleness, and patience?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) transmits a saying of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) describing a hierarchical chain of virtues that support one another: faith is served by knowledge, knowledge is served by forbearance, forbearance is served by gentleness, and gentleness is served by patience. The term 'vizier' (wazir) — the chief minister of a caliph — is used metaphorically to convey that each virtue acts as the essential support and complement to the one preceding it, without which the higher virtue cannot function effectively.
